Adapt the inverse-distance-cube correction from the separately measured, correct arithmetic trial (0.0012955 s): compute r=rsqrtf(distSq), e=fmaf(distSq,r*r,-1.0f), and use (r*r*r)*fmaf(-1.5f,e,1.0f) for the inverse cube. Guard r==0 before computing e so infinite distSq cannot produce NaN. Apply this to the original mass numerator; do not also cancel target mass or alter tiling, synchronization, self-exclusion, or integration. Keep the base launch configuration unchanged. Recompile and run the full correctness suite and official timing; the combination is unmeasured.

decision.rationale: Read the complete kernel source for the fastest supplied valid candidate before selecting an integration; the evidence reports 128 threads and a 256-entry shared tile.

Use the fastest supplied valid base: the shared-memory 256-source tile candidate (0.0008920 s versus baseline 0.0018473 s). Adapt the inverse-distance-cube correction from the separately measured, correct arithmetic trial (0.0012955 s): compute r=rsqrtf(distSq), e=fmaf(distSq,r*r,-1.0f), and use (r*r*r)*fmaf(-1.5f,e,1.0f) for the inverse cube. Guard r==0 before computing e so infinite distSq cannot produce NaN. Apply this to the original mass numerator; do not also cancel target mass or alter tiling, synchronization, self-exclusion, or integration. Keep the base launch configuration unchanged. Recompile and run the full correctness suite and official timing; the combination is unmeasured.

The first integration is correct and improved mean time to 0.0006500 s. Search the next diverse archive page for other measured, compatible transformations before choosing whether another combination is worthwhile.
